title: Use ordinary gauge structure without calling the bare pair transparent
statement: If a pair's admitted nominal data-apparatus operators commute with Zi,Zj, arbitrary apparatus faults induce data Kraus operators in Alg(Zi,Zj)=span{I,Zi}*Alg(S), S=ZiZj. One participating data-qubit/apparatus fault lies in span{I,Xi,Yi,Zi}*Alg(S), including coherent faults and records. When S is an actual subsystem gauge generator, this is one correctable physical error modulo gauge, despite the severe bare-pair disturbance. Initial apparatus cannot contain uncounted prior logical correlations. Leakage, arbitrary cross-pair faults and simultaneous noncommuting couplings are excluded. The conventional 3x3 Bacon-Shor proof and a 100-error/10,000-product finite subsystem-KL check support this containment. It alone supplies neither trustworthy reports nor physical recovery. Persistent hot apparatus reused on other pairs requires actual reset, dedication or joint memory analysis.
